title: Pinehaven Bakery conversational pilot scratchpad
content:
Quick context: Pinehaven is a small regional bakery chain (35 stores, mostly in suburbs). They want a conversational kiosk/assistant to help in-store customers (menu, allergens, order status) and a lightweight web chat for same-day pickup. Pilot scope: 6 stores -> 4 kiosks + web widget; 3-month pilot. Main constraints from call: strict PII rules (no logged phone numbers), intermittent store WiFi (8/35 stores previously flagged as flaky), prefer on-prem or VPC for auditability, low latency (target p90 < 350ms for short Q/A flows), and cost sensitivity (won't accept expensive per-token ops).

Call attendees (11/11): Pinehaven - Sara Cole (Ops), Ethan Wu (IT manager), Priya (customer success), Marco (solutions eng), Zoe (PM). Notes:
- Sara: top ask is accurate allergen answers and clarifying cross-contamination policies (legal sensitive).
- Ethan: wants VPC deployment; can run 2x A10G-equivalent GPUs in small datacenter rack, but bandwidth to cloud is limited.
- Sara: offline fallback must be local FAQ cached on kiosk.
- Ethan: willing to accept quantized model if it meets accuracy bar.
- Mentioned prior vendor dropped due to hallucinations about recipes -> high trust requirement.

Primary goals (pilot success criteria):
- Accuracy: Allergen answers correct & references (if model provides assertions, must include source lines or fallback to canned responses).
- Latency: interactive feel on kiosk — p95 < 500ms acceptable, ideal p90 < 350ms.
- Reliability: kiosk should still answer basic FAQs when disconnected.
- Cost: pilot budget cap = $2.5k/mo on inference.
- Observability: Pinehaven must see per-interaction logs (non-PII) and top prompt errors.

Technical constraints / gotchas called out:
- Network: intermittent NAT and packet loss; cannot rely on large round-trip dependency to hosted API for kiosk. Suggest private deployment or hybrid: model on-prem, control plane in VPC.
- Data retention: legal prohibits storing phone numbers and customer notes beyond 7 days. We'll need to redact and not log PII.
- UI: kiosk uses small ARM box (Odroid-like) as frontend; it will call local inference endpoint over LAN. Need small binary for local health check and fallback static FAQ.
- Hardware: Pinehaven has 2 available GPUs per site (older generation) but only 2 stores have GPU capable infrastructure. For pilot, propose colocated mini-datacenter with 2x A10G on a managed rack we provision in region close to stores -> reduces network variance.
- Prompting: short Q/A vs multi-turn ordering. For ordering flow, must avoid open-ended generation; prefer structured form filling (slots) and server-side verification to prevent weird outputs.

Model ideas and tradeoffs:
- Candidate: 7B quantized open model with Redwood runtime optimizations (low cost, good for short Q/A). Risk: hallucination frequency may still be > Pinehaven's tolerance for allergen queries.
- Alternate: 13B medium-pruned + selective retrieval for policy/regulatory text (store SOP) — heavier but produce citations.
- Fallback: server-held canned FAQ answers for any question with low model confidence. Confidence threshold tuning is critical.

Prompt patterns / examples (notes-to-self):
- System: "You are a concise, safety-first assistant for Pinehaven Bakery staff and customers. If unsure, say 'I don't know, let me check' and pass to POS or canned FAQ."
- Customer prompt example: "Does your almond croissant contain peanuts?" -> plan: chain-retrieval: look up ingredient table -> if not found, reply canned "Please ask a team member" + escalate flag.
- Multi-turn ordering: always return JSON slot object: {order_items:[{id,qty}], pickup_time, modifiers} (we'll generate schema server-side, do not accept freeform addresses).

Observability / metrics we need to show Pinehaven:
- Per-route latency histograms (kiosk vs web).
- Model confidence distribution and frequency of canned-fallback triggers.
- Rate of PII redactions.
- Top 10 unanswered queries (for FAQ growth).

Privacy & compliance notes:
- Default: do not persist request text for 7 days; after that truncate to metadata only. Need to show Pinehaven retention controls in Console.
- PII redaction: front-end should regex-strip phone numbers/emails before sending. Also server-side detectors to catch missed items.
- Audit log: include interaction id, route, timestamp, model version, but store redacted transcripts.

Operational plan (pilot phases):
1) Week 0–2: Prep — ingest Pinehaven menu, SOPs, allergen tables. Build canned FAQ pack and web widget stub.
2) Week 2–4: Deploy private inference cluster in colocated rack (or VPC depending on final infra). Roll model v0 (quantized 7B) for kiosk read-only mode.
3) Week 4–8: Enable structured ordering in web widget only. Monitor hallucinations and fallback rates.
4) Week 8–12: Expand to 4 kiosks, iterate prompt tuning, run customer satisfaction survey.

Action items (owners):
- Marco: get hardware compatibility checklist from Pinehaven (due 2024-11-18).
- Zoe: assemble FAQ + SOP ingestion list and map to schema for retrieval (due 2024-11-20).
- Priya: draft privacy/retention clause for pilot contract (due 2024-11-22).
- Ethan (customer): provide sample POS webhook and order schema (due 2024-11-19).
- Me (Priya): run quick perf sim with quantized-7B on A10G to validate p95 target (aim to complete by 2024-11-25).

Risks / open questions:
- Hallucination tolerance: what percent is acceptable? Pinehaven said "very low" but not concrete — need target (e.g., <1% for allergen Qs).
- Where to host logs/analytics? They want visibility but not raw transcripts. Do we offer a filtered dashboard or export?
- GPU availability: if they cannot give GPUs in-site, budget/ops might prefer Redwood Dedicated. Need quick cost estimate for dedicated pool for pilot.
- Edge device compute: kiosk frontends are ARM boxes; local models may need conversion/edge runtime. We should push compute to local rack instead of kiosk to avoid ARM constraints.

Random brainstorming / heuristics to try in pilot:
- Use retrieval-augmented answers with explicit source lines (SOP page + ingredients sheet) to reduce hallucinations.
- Hard-block certain topics (recipes, pricing negotiation) to canned responses.
- Telemetry: capture token counts per interaction to estimate monthly cost and compare to $2.5k cap.
- Consider light-weight intent classifier on-edge to route simple queries to cached FAQ vs full model for lower cost and latency.

Notes-to-self (short):
- Keep conversation transcripts for debugging in secure bucket for 7d; after 7d, keep only hashed query + metadata.
- Prepare 2 model configs: low-latency (aggressive quant, constrained context) and high-accuracy (larger model + retrieval) for A/B.
- Add explicit tests for allergen Qs to our eval harness; get sample 50 queries from Pinehaven Ops.

Next meeting: sync w/ Ethan + Sara week of 2024-11-25 to finalize infra choice (on-prem vs dedicated). Prep items: quick perf numbers, draft retention clause, hardware checklist.

End of scratchpad.

---

Trailing messy bits (raw ideas):
- Maybe provide a "manager mode" in kiosk to fetch manager contact but masked; only show last 4 digits of phone for staff.
- If network flaps, kiosk enters offline mode and serves top-20 FAQs locally; log events for sync.
- If model returns low-confidence for allergen, automatically append: "Please confirm with staff — allergy info on file X" (force staff handoff).

(That's probably enough for now — keep iterative and keep record of each prompt change when we tune.)
